Meta and Microsoft — two of the largest and spendiest companies in the world — are slated to report earnings results after the close today at a time when investors are feeling increasingly queasy about the amounts Big Tech is spending on artificial intelligence. Last week, Google ’s parent reported capital expenditures above its previous forecast, making for its first cash-flow negative quarter since it went public in 2004. The company said its spending is aimed at meeting a growing backlog of cloud contracts. Still, that news dragged down other hyperscalers, including Meta and Microsoft, as well as the broader market. Microsoft is expected to keep its free cash flow in the green. Meanwhile, analysts are expecting Meta to report its first free cash-flow negative quarter since 2012. Here is what the two have guided for capex as of their last report: Microsoft — which will be reporting its fiscal Q4 results — said in its last report that it expects to spend $190 billion in capital expenditures this calendar year. Meta (whose fiscal calendar overlaps with the normal calendar year) set its guidance for 2026 capex at between $125 and 145 billion . I’m old enough to remember when investors were excited about big spending on capex, seeing it as both proof that a company is staying on the cutting edge and as a promise of future demand. Now they seem more eager to see money coming in, not out. “In our view, investors are becoming less willing to reward higher AI spending on its own and are increasingly looking for progress in earning a return on that investment,” said Brian Therien, a senior analyst at Edward Jones. title: 💡 Marketplace of ideas
body_text: “Waiter, there’s an ant in my sorbet!” may sound like the start of a tired joke, but it’s actually the basis of a very serious and real criminal case in South Korea, where authorities arrested a top chef with two Michelin stars in connection with serving up ant-sprinkled desserts. Despite customers' awareness of the insects in their orders, prosecutors are reportedly seeking a one-year sentence for the chef and a 20 million won (~$14,000) fine for the Seoul restaurant, owing to the fact that ants aren’t one of the 10 insects approved for human consumption in South Korea. Whether you’re looking to furnish your new apartment with vintage furniture, hunting for an instrument to help finally realize your longstanding musical ambitions, or simply trying to offload the clothes that your kids (or you) have long grown out of, Facebook Marketplace has become one of the go-to platforms for buying and selling pre-loved goods. Now, Meta is making it even easier for the site’s sellers to make listings and manage their offers, announcing the “Seller” app at the end of last week. The new app comes with a dedicated suite of tools such as a built-in inbox, new AI listing capabilities, and listing performance analytics. Given Marketplace’s growth in recent years — it has ballooned to 430 million monthly listings and now counts 1.1 billion active users — it’s little wonder that Meta is looking to expand on one of the true business bright spots across its sprawling online empire. Per Google Trends data, search interest in Facebook Marketplace has soared far ahead of that for its Messenger platform in the US; it even overtook searches to login to the site overall in early 2023, as more Americans look to Marketplace to buy and sell online. Even though Marketplace has shone as a jewel in Meta’s internet crown for a while now (traffic was up 15% year-over-year in 2024, compared to a 3.6% decline across the broader Facebook.com domain), the carved-out app feels like a notable step up for the platform, expanding its position as an ecommerce behemoth and building on a partnership it announced with legacy industry titan eBay last year . 📺 Big Brother: Markets are currently pricing contestant Dee Valladares as the favorite to win “Big Brother” season 28 at an 18% chance of victory. * Other strong contenders include Barrett Pfeiffer (11%), Rick Devens (14%) and Kamu Kirk (10%). 🎬 Paramount: The news last week that Paramount agreed to delay its merger with Warner Bros. for “months” has upended markets that had for months been bullish on Paramount’s chances at completing the merger; the probability that nobody buys Warner jumped from 15% to 29% over the weekend . *Event contracts are offered through Robinhood Derivatives, LLC — probabilities referenced or sourced from KalshiEx LLC or ForecastEx LLC. title: 🟢 Peptides get the green light
body_text: Being out of a job is no fun, but it’s happened to the best of us. Even Mr. Incredible (the father in the 2004 Pixar film, The Incredibles) was let go from his job at an insurance firm before saving the day. Unfortunately for about 108 employees at Pixar, Mrs. Incredible helped deliver the news that they may soon be out of a job, sitting on the letterhead used by the company to inform regulators. Stocks finished flat Friday, with the S&P 500 virtually unchanged while the Nasdaq dropped about half a point. Last week, the US Food and Drug Administration voted to loosen restrictions on a slew of peptides so that compounding pharmacies can dispense bespoke mixes of them. As of now, consumers are bypassing the FDA by buying vials of peptides labeled “for research use only ” and then conducting that research on themselves, to put it euphemistically. The move (which is non-binding, but jibes with the stated will of the agency’s leadership ) is a massive win for the telehealth industry, which has been eager to pounce on the opportunity to sell yet another product in a vial to consumers seeking to live longer and look hotter. Unlike FDA approved drugs, there isn’t much literature on the safety or efficacy of the substances that will soon be flooding telehealth sites — and, if the GLP-1 craze is any indicator — Instagram and TikTok feeds. BPC-157, one popular peptide said to have regenerative effects, is probably the most widely studied and even it has not had thorough studies done on humans. On the other hand, some (mostly those who want to sell peptides) argue, if people are injecting themselves with unproven and potentially unsafe substances anyways, why not hold suppliers to basic safety standards as opposed to letting a grey market thrive? Once these peptides get the FDA’s official blessing, it opens up a new consumer unit for telehealth companies. The main two players in the public markets are Hims & Hers and Enhanced Group — both rallied after the vote. Similar to telehealth’s relationship with knock-off GLP-1s, the idea is patients are drawn into the service seeking a certain drug, they talk to a doctor or nurse, and voilà — a small glass vial and needles arrive at your door and live in your fridge. It’s unclear how big a market we’re talkin’. The global peptide therapeutics market is valued at approximately $52 billion today and projected to reach $87 billion by 2035, according to one estimate from Precedence Research . Enhanced Group ( the company behind the Enhanced Games ) has said that it’s ready to go. In its most recent earnings call in May, Hims CEO Andrew Dudum didn’t give a firm timeline on rolling out that segment but said, “We likely won’t be first to market.” 📊 Elections: The race to watch in the remaining primaries for this midterm election is quickly becoming the Wisconsin Democratic governor election, which has seen candidates jump in and drop out over the past several weeks as the establishment failed to coalesce around a chosen candidate.
